structure.title: A duplicated proposal
structure.text: Falstaff's approach gives two women a shared opportunity to compare his intentions and arrange a response.

structure.title: Household counterplots
structure.text: Jealousy, courtship, and practical jokes overlap as several people attempt to direct events without knowing others' plans.

people.name: Falstaff
people.text: A broke, boastful old knight who decides to woo two wealthy married women at once in the hope of getting at their husbands' money.

people.name: Mistress Ford and Mistress Page
people.text: Two friends in Windsor who discover they have received identical love letters from Falstaff and set out to teach him a lesson.

people.name: Ford
people.text: Mistress Ford's husband, so jealous that he disguises himself to spy on Falstaff, and nearly ruins the wives' joke.

context.title: Domestic intelligence
context.text: The women know their households and neighbours better than Falstaff expects. Ordinary social coordination becomes a source of power.

context.title: Town comedy
context.text: Money, marriage, and local reputation matter more than national affairs. Characters compete over access to household resources.
context.takeaway: Follow the practical purpose of each scheme.

notice.text: Notice repeated attempts with new disguises.
notice.why: Falstaff's confidence survives evidence that should correct it.

notice.text: Compare justified suspicion with jealous invention.
notice.why: Different people reach similar accusations for different reasons.

opening: Falstaff decides to improve his finances by seducing two married women who can access their husbands' money. He economises on effort by sending them nearly identical letters. Unfortunately for him, the women compare notes and find the proposal more useful as entertainment than temptation. Shakespeare brings his great opportunist into a town where household intelligence can defeat swagger, while a jealous husband supplies additional confusion. The comedy belongs to people who understand exactly how they are being underestimated and decide to make the experience expensive.
